review.selectedRoute: Adapt the verified normalized analytic derivative/q-Euler proof using native analytic power-series differentiation. Reuse the local bounded-derivative theorem, original j times discriminant identity and native level-one weight-14 dimension argument. The constructed nonzero scalar yields the exact sixth-power identity, sufficient to scale the already proved arithmetic-subgroup norm integral equation. No new norm polynomial, Ramanujan system, Fourier integration-by-parts, higher-weight cusp power generalization or prescribed scalar assumption.
review.assumptionsToDischarge: For any finite-index integral subgroup containing T, an actual weight-two cusp form f and a Laurent coefficient Y with Y*qEuler(j)=qExpansion(f), the exact expression Y^6*j^4*(j-1728)^3 is integral over C[j]. The integral equation and analytic/formal derivative normalization are derived, not hypotheses. The same theorem applies to Gamma1 and its Hecke correspondence subgroup.
